```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5.5)
```

The package evaluates supplied probabilities. Start with predictions from held-out
or otherwise appropriate evaluation data. The package cannot determine whether
the evaluation data were also used for model fitting or threshold selection.

## Inputs and the positive class

```{r}
library(healthmlaudit)
head(demo_predictions)
```

These 400 observations are simulated. The identifiers do not refer to real
patients. Outcomes are independent Bernoulli draws from logistic probabilities;
the predicted probabilities use a modified score to illustrate imperfect
calibration. The two group labels are synthetic, and no model is trained here.

```{r}
audit <- audit_binary(
  demo_predictions, truth = "outcome", prob = "predicted_risk",
  positive = 1, threshold = 0.5
)
audit
```

`positive` determines the event class. The probabilities must refer to that class.
A factor's first level does not override this choice. The classification rule is
probability greater than or equal to the threshold.

AUROC describes ranking across positive and negative observations. Accuracy,
sensitivity, specificity, and precision describe predictions at the chosen
threshold. Brier score measures squared probability error; smaller values are
better. A high AUROC does not imply reliable probabilities.

## Inspect calibration

```{r}
calibration <- plot_calibration(audit, bins = 8)
calibration
calibration$data
```

Each point describes an occupied equal-width interval. Points below the diagonal
have lower observed event proportions than mean predicted probabilities, while
points above it have higher proportions. Point size shows the bin count.
The pattern depends on the binning choice, and the graph is descriptive. It is
not a significance test or a demonstration of clinical usefulness.

## Compare subgroups

```{r}
groups <- audit_subgroups(audit, group = "age_group", min_n = 30)
groups[c("group", "n", "positive_n", "negative_n", "prevalence", "roc_auc", "brier", "warnings")]
```

The same positive class and threshold apply to both groups. Check their event
counts as well as their metrics. Differences in prevalence, sampling, or other
characteristics can affect performance summaries; a subgroup difference alone
does not establish unfairness or a causal effect.

Missing group labels are retained in a separate NA group. `min_n` flags small
groups but is not a statistical sufficiency rule. A single-class group has an
undefined AUROC, returned as NA with an explanation.

## Estimate uncertainty

```{r}
intervals <- bootstrap_ci(audit, metrics = c("roc_auc", "brier"),
                          times = 500, conf_level = .95, seed = 42)
intervals
```

The bootstrap samples whole rows, keeping the outcome and probability paired.
Percentile limits use type-7 quantiles. The output records requested, valid,
and invalid replicates separately for each metric. A one-class resample cannot
estimate AUROC. Its AUROC is excluded from the interval calculation and counted
as invalid; a defined Brier score from that same resample is retained.

These intervals assume independent observations. They do not account for model
retraining, dependence between repeated patient records, or selection of a
threshold on the same data. Small samples, rare outcomes, and many invalid
replicates may make the intervals unreliable. Increase `times` for greater
Monte Carlo stability, but do not treat more resamples as a substitute for more
evaluation observations.

## Missing or invalid inputs

```{r}
with_missing <- demo_predictions
with_missing$predicted_risk[1] <- NA
tryCatch(audit_binary(with_missing, "outcome", "predicted_risk"),
         error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```

Explicit omission records what was removed and leaves unrelated columns alone:

```{r}
omitted <- audit_binary(with_missing, "outcome", "predicted_risk", na_action = "omit")
omitted$metadata[c("n_input", "n_used", "n_omitted", "omitted_rows")]
```

Probabilities outside [0, 1], infinite values, and more than two classes are
errors. The omission option does not excuse invalid observed values.

## Save a report

```{r}
files <- generate_report(audit, groups, intervals,
                          file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"))
all(file.exists(unlist(files)))
```

For a file in the current directory, use `file = "model_audit.md"`. The report
references a calibration PNG saved beside it, so share the two files together.
The output contains aggregate results and warnings, not individual predictions.
Use `overwrite = TRUE` only when replacing an existing report is intended.

## References

The standard metrics are calculated with [yardstick](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/).
See its documentation for [AUROC](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/reference/roc_auc.html),
[Brier score](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/reference/brier_class.html), and
[classification metrics](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/reference/sens.html).
The contribution here is the shared input contract, result handling, and audit
workflow. The package does not introduce a new metric or a new bootstrap method.
